C9.2.quote: at each round the voters report their preferences over the available candidates
C9.2.note: Needed: approval sets reflect what voters care about (stated, without reason, via voters reporting their preferences) and satisfaction defined from approvals (stated in Section 2). No strategic or information assumptions are needed since no strategic analysis is drawn on.

C1.reason: Besides the complexity results (AL), Theorem 7.1 (GCR provides EJR) and Proposition 7.4 (no rule satisfies EJR semi-online) are main results on which rules satisfy which properties, so AX also applies; AL remains primary.

C2.4.reason: The abstract states that voters report their preferences, a statement that the submitted approval sets equal held preferences with no reason given, which excludes IDU (no statement about reporting) and fits IDS.

C3.2.reason: Consistent with C2.4 = IDS, the paper says in words that voters report their preferences, so the non-strategic analysis has a stated sincerity assumption.

C3.3.reason: C3.2 = STATED and no reason (strategyproofness, incentives, convention) is given for voters reporting their preferences.

C5.2.reason: JR/PJR/EJR and satisfaction are evaluated on the approval sets, which the paper states are the voters' reported preferences (C2.4 = IDS), giving INPUT-STATED.

C6.VOT.reason: Voters take a fixed action in the model (reporting approval sets each round), which the codebook counts as present with NONSTRAT behaviour stated in words.

C9.2.reason: The needed assumptions (approval sets reflect voters' preferences; satisfaction defined from approvals) are stated via voters reporting their preferences and the satisfaction definition, so ALL-STATED is consistent with C2.4 = IDS.
